articles.headline: NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 11, plus non-QB MVPs
articles.description: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 11? We made our 1-32 list and picked the non-quarterback MVPs for each roster.
articles.headlineJa: NFLパワーランキング：第11週に向けた全32チームの格付け、およびQB以外のMVP選出
articles.descriptionJa: 第11週を控えたNFL全チームの勢力図はどうなっているでしょうか？全32チームを1位から32位までランク付けし、各チームのQB以外のMVPを選出しました。
articles.body:
When the NFL Honors awards ceremony takes place the Thursday before Super Bowl LXI, it's almost guaranteed that the player who accepts the MVP award will be a quarterback. Former Vikings running back Adrian Peterson is the only non-QB to be named MVP since 2010, and only three non-QBs have won in the 21st century.

But what if quarterbacks were disqualified from winning the award? In addition to our weekly 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick the non-quarterback MVP for each team at midseason. Which defenders and skill players deserve love for what they've done this season?

To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a couple of highlights from this week's rankings:

The Patriots' trip to Munich could not have gone any worse, as they left Germany with a two-game losing streak and without quarterback Drake Maye (ankle injury). That caused them to fall the most out of any team in our Power Rankings compared to last week (three spots), and Maye could be out for the season if his ankle is fractured. New England is 1-3 in its past four games, with all of its losses coming to NFC North opponents.

The Browns are in the top 15 of our rankings for the first time this season after another comeback win -- this time against the Texans. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson has conducted a winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime in all six of the Browns' wins. Watson joins the Cowboys' Troy Aikman (1990) and Lions' Matthew Stafford (2016) as the only QBs in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to achieve that feat, per ESPN Research.

The Commanders made the biggest climb of any team this week (three spots) after a Thursday night win over the Giants. Washington is 2-1 since its bye week, and it's still not out of the NFC East race yet, two games behind first-place New York while owning the head-to-head tiebreaker with the Giants. However, the Commanders have only one divisional game left to boost their playoff odds -- Week 18 versus the Cowboys.

Let's get into the full list, starting with a slight change at No. 1 from last week.

1. San Francisco 49ers (8-1)

Week 10 result: Beat the Cowboys 46-40

Week 10 ranking: 2

Non-QB MVP at midseason: LB Fred Warner

While QB Brock Purdy is a top candidate for league MVP, Warner is making a strong case to be the first linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year since Luke Kuechly in 2013. Warner's 88 tackles rank sixth in the NFL. He's tied for first in forced fumbles (five) to go with a fumble recovery, 0.5 sacks and three pass breakups. articles.headline: What the NBA's first month has revealed about all 30 teams
articles.description: With the season's first month nearly in the books, Ben Golliver examines the biggest storyline so far for all 30 teams.
articles.headlineJa: NBA開幕初月で分かった全30チームの現状
articles.descriptionJa: シーズンの最初の1ヶ月がほぼ終了した今、ベン・ゴリバーが全30チームについて、これまでの最大の注目ポイントを検証します。
articles.body:
The NBA season is a month old, which makes this a natural time to take stock of all 30 teams.

The San Antonio Spurs, Los Angeles Lakers, Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics sit atop the standings, the defending champion New York Knicks are treading water and several aspiring contenders are juggling star injuries.

And even though Thanksgiving is still more than a week away, the Oklahoma City Thunder have already executed a rare early-season trade and the New Orleans Pelicans have already fielded a public trade request.

With so many developments to wade through, here's what we've learned about all 30 teams since opening night.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks

The first month revealed ... Kingston Flemings is a great fit

To no great surprise, Hawks coach Quin Snyder opened the season with a starting lineup -- Nickeil Alexander-Walker, CJ McCollum, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu -- that boasted a phenomenal plus-20.3 net rating in 391 minutes in 2025-26. That decision, which favored experience and continuity, left 2026 lottery pick Flemings and offseason trade acquisitions Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins as reserves.

But Atlanta's starters weren't nearly as potent on offense in the early going as they were last season, so Snyder rejiggered his lineup by replacing the 35-year-old McCollum with the 19-year-old Flemings after only eight games. Atlanta's starters have played at a faster pace and boasted a stingier defense since the move, albeit in a small sample size.

Though Flemings is unlikely to generate Rookie of the Year buzz with several of his draft classmates posting huge numbers, he should be in the All-Rookie mix because he already has distinguished himself in a veteran-dominated rotation with serious playoff aspirations.

The No. 8 pick fits Atlanta's blueprint perfectly: He's confident on the ball but doesn't overly dominate possessions, he can space the court with a dependable outside shot, and he's a pesky defender who thrives in an up-tempo style.

Boston Celtics

The first month revealed ... There is life after Jaylen Brown

Boston's blockbuster summer trade of Brown to Philadelphia for Paul George was met with shock, sadness and anger in some corners of the Celtics' fanbase. Brown stoked those hard feelings last month by playing up the tension with former teammate Jayson Tatum: "There's no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy."

Unfortunately for Brown, he played like Hamburger Helper in his first game against his former team last week, a blowout victory for the Celtics. Though that high-profile showdown wasn't representative of Philadelphia's strong start, it was further proof that Boston has moved on smoothly after the breakup. As of Tuesday, the Celtics boast the East's best offensive rating and point differential.

articles.headline: Fantasy football: Live Week 11 free agent pickups advice with ESPN expert
articles.description: ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody is here to answer your pressing questions live from noon to 1 p.m. ET.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール：ESPNの専門家が教える第11週のフリーエージェント獲得アドバイス（ライブ）
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNのファンタジー・フットボール専門家エリック・ムーディが、東部標準時正午から午後1時まで、皆さんの切実な質問にライブでお答えします。
articles.body:
With six teams off this week -- the Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks -- all thanks to the latest occurrence of Bye-mageddon, your fantasy team probably has a lot more holes to fill than usual.

And it's not just Week 11 you need to be concerned about. If you've been relying on Patriots QB Drake Maye, you're going to have to make a move today to prepare for Week 12 as Maye has a broken ankle and could potentially miss the rest of season.

Fear not! Our ESPN fantasy football expert will be here live from noon to 1 p.m. ET, just as he will be every Tuesday of the NFL's regular season, to try and answer all of your waiver wire questions and other fantasy-related queries. 

Which surprises from last weekend's games are worth picking up in your league? Should you drop the player that has disappointed you so far? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Eric Moody has answers.

He will do his best to try and answer as many questions as he can to get you and your fantasy team ready for this week's action. 

More advice: Week 11 free agent pickups | Week 11 rankings

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.description: Manchester United are among the clubs interested in Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw. Transfer Talk has the latest.

articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは、ニューカッスル・ユナイテッドのセンターバック、マリック・ティアウに関心を示すクラブの一つです。「トランスファー・トーク」が最新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw is on the radar of Manchester United, while AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are among the clubs interested in Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw, according to Sky Germany. Despite establishing himself as a key figure in the Magpies' backline, the 25-year-old Germany international could be available next summer, although Newcastle would demand at least an €80 million fee for his signature. However, Newcastle will reject any January offers for left back Lewis Hall amid longstanding interest from United, according to The Telegraph. The 22-year-old was the subject of an enquiry from the Red Devils last summer before signing a new long-term contract in September.

- AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus ahead of the January transfer window, Calciomercato has reported. The USMNT striker's agent Jorge Mendes has contacted both clubs, who are looking to strengthen their attacking options, after a €40 million move to Everton collapsed at the end of the last window. The 25-year-old, who is under contract at Monaco until June 2028, is reportedly open to the idea of playing in Serie A.

- Real Madrid are weighing up a move to bring Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Chema Andrés back to the club, as per TEAMtalk. Chema, 21, came through the Madrid youth team ranks but left in 2025 and has impressed since arriving at VfB Stuttgart in the summer. However, a deal could be complicated as there is uncertainty over his contractual situation, with Brighton previously disputing suggestions that Madrid retain an option to re-sign him permanently. Madrid also monitoring highly-rated Brighton defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined from Tottenham Hotspur for £46 million this summer.

- Manchester City defender Josko Gvardiol is on the radar of Barcelona, according to AS. Gvardiol, 24, has become one of the best young defenders in Europe in recent years and Barca are keen to strengthen their defensive options. However, while the club are interested in signing the Croatia international, they do not think a deal will be possible unless he pushes to leave amid the fallout from City's financial charges.

- Bayern Munich youth goalkeeper Leonard Prescott could leave  on a free transfer next summer, after contract talks stalled, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Brighton and Aston Villa are among the clubs tracking his development, says Sky Germany. Prescott, 17, was born in New York but has represented Germany at U17 and is very highly rated.

articles.headline: The clock is ticking on Steph Curry's final act with the Warriors
articles.description: At 38, Curry is still brilliant -- but managing his body has become the biggest battle of his career.
articles.headlineJa: ステフィン・カリー、ウォリアーズでの「ラストダンス」へのカウントダウン
articles.descriptionJa: 38歳となったカリーは依然として輝きを放っているが、身体のコンディション管理がキャリア最大の戦いとなっている。
articles.body:
LATE LAST JANUARY, during an off-day workout in an empty downtown Minneapolis arena, Stephen Curry's right knee started bothering him.

Four days prior, he had been named an All-Star starter for an 11th time, averaging 27.2 points on extreme efficiency, keeping the Golden State Warriors' record at a respectable 25-21.

But his co-star, Jimmy Butler, had torn his right ACL the week before. Curry, at 37, was again dealing with overloaded schemes and an increased offensive burden. His knee started barking.

"That was the moment where I started to get concerned," Curry said. "It just didn't feel right."

Curry attempted to play through what he described as "a weird soreness and pain that didn't go away." Despite being initially listed as questionable, he had 26 points against the Timberwolves, rested for a game and then scored 27 in Utah to close the road trip and 23 against the Detroit Pistons once the team returned home.

But neither the pain nor concern would subside.

"Against Detroit, it took everything in me down there on the training table just to be like, 'Oh, I can go out here tonight and play,'" Curry said. "And I was just faking it for the first whatever [25 minutes]."

There's something poetic about his final sequence before he left the game. Curry came off a third-quarter pindown into an isolation against Ausar Thompson and did what he described as "a high-step thing because it hurt so bad in that moment."

After the fidget, Curry shook Thompson with a crossover combination, hobbled into the lane and poured in an and-1 floater over one of the best perimeter defenders in the world to give him 23 points in those 25 minutes.

But then he limped to the sideline and told Rick Celebrini -- the franchise's lead medical decision-maker whom Curry trusts implicitly -- that the swelling and stiffness had become too much to bear.

"I got smart about the situation," said Curry, who missed the next 27 games. "We had to go get scans."

This is the dichotomy of the still-spectacular Curry in the twilight stage of his Hall of Fame career. On the court, he can still string together what coach Steve Kerr calls "magical" performances.

But away from the fireworks show, Curry is in a constant race against time, obsessively evolving his body-maintenance plan in an effort to be available as often as possible -- until the clock runs out.

Ten days ago, Curry sat down with ESPN to discuss the physical and mental challenges of the moment, mostly centered on the management of a knee injury that derailed his 17th season -- and led to the Warriors tumbling to 37-45 and missing the playoffs.

One night after the conversation, he scorched the Orlando Magic for 41 points, surpassing LeBron James and Michael Jordan for the most 40-point games after age 35 in NBA history, continuing a surge that spiked the Warriors' record to 8-3 and indicated his offensive game was as sharp as ever.

articles.headline: Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 11: Takes on four QBs, Lions, Rams, more
articles.description: Get ready for Week 11 with what makes Vikings-49ers must-watch football, Joe Burrow's MVP case and how Aidan Hutchinson's injury could impact the Lions.
articles.headlineJa: ソラックが考えるNFL第11週の7つの注目点：4人のQB、ライオンズ、ラムズ、その他
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングス対49ersが必見の試合である理由、ジョー・バロウのMVP争い、エイダン・ハッチンソンの負傷がライオンズに与える影響など、第11週に向けて準備しよう。
articles.body:
Are you excited for NFL Week 11? At first, it might look like a sleepy slate. Jaguars at Giants and Raiders at Broncos are two of our marquee games. But there's one contest that, to this enormous football nerd, is the game of the season.

Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide'

This week, I'll expand on why Joe Burrow looks like an MVP, tell you about another Rams personnel innovation, project eventual QB changes for two NFC South teams and wonder if Aidan Hutchinson is the final defensive injury the Lions can't overcome. But first, here's one matchup you won't want to miss.

Jump to:

Shanahan vs. Flores is matchup of the best 

Why Burrow is the MVP

Rams should lean on their RBs

Hutchinson's injury wounds Lions bad 

Do Falcons need a new 2027 QB?

Do Saints need a new 2027 QB?

Mendoza's debut is a scratch

Some extra inklings

I think ... Vikings-49ers is the coolest game of the season

The Vikings have had a fraught three weeks. Everyone was excited to see them face the Lions in Week 8 -- the best offense they'd faced in a while. Detroit stuck it to 'em with a sick schematic wrinkle for which the Vikings were not prepared -- multiple tight ends lined up in the backfield as quasi-fullbacks to pave open rushing lanes.

Then the Vikings played the Bills in Week 9 -- Josh Allen and another grindy running game -- and the Packers in Week 10 with Jordan Love coming off a flamethrower performance against the Patriots. At various points over those three weeks, it has felt like the upcoming test for the Vikings has been the test for the Vikings. Will this be the offense to build a blueprint against Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unique defense? Or will Flores prove that his defense is insurmountable even by the league's top attacks?

The NFL rarely exists in such absolutes. All of those particular matchups were exciting and educational in their own ways. But if there's one game I've been waiting for with bated breath in the seasonlong pursuit of an answer to the Flores defense, it's this one: Vikings against 49ers in Week 11.

This is quite literally the best against the best. The 49ers lead the league in points per drive (3.0), success rate and EPA per play on offense. The Vikings lead the league in points per drive (1.24), success rate and EPA per play (if you eliminate the Bucs' rainstorm game against the Falcons, which is cheating, but I don't care) on defense. articles.headline: Emmett Johnson, Jaxon Smith-Njigba shine in big offensive week for Africa's NFL stars
articles.description: Week 10 in the 2026 NFL season was one of the most noteworthy in terms of standout performances from offensive players in the NFL with known African ties.
articles.headlineJa: アフリカにルーツを持つNFLスターが活躍、エメット・ジョンソンとジャクソン・スミス＝ニジバが攻撃陣で輝く
articles.descriptionJa: 2026年NFLシーズン第10週は、アフリカにゆかりのあるNFLオフェンシブプレーヤーたちの目覚ましい活躍において、最も注目すべき週の一つとなった。
articles.body:
Week 10 in the 2026 NFL season was one of the most noteworthy in terms of standout performances from offensive players in the NFL with known African ties.

Last season's Offensive Player of the Year, Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who proudly represents Sierra Leone due to a connection to the country through his grandparents - is no stranger to prominence in our weekly recaps. However, the Seattle Seahawks wide receiver was not alone in delivering a huge performance over the past week.

Emmett Johnson, who is of Liberian descent, had a memorable weekend for the Kansas City Chiefs, while Chuba Hubbard - who has Nigerian ties - was crucial in the Carolina Panthers' win over the New Orleans Saints.

Africa Player of the Week: Emmett Johnson (Kansas City Chiefs)

Johnson - a running back who grew up in Minneapolis and was born to parents who moved from Liberia - made a mammoth contribution to the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons in his first NFL start.

Johnson tallied a total of 171 yards - 101 yards across 22 carries and 70 more across six receptions - with two receiving touchdowns.

The 23-year-old chipped at the Falcons defense bit by bit rather than looking to tear them apart all at once. His longest reception was for 34 yards, but he was ruthlessly efficient and scored touchdowns in both the first and last quarters.

This was the third game in a row in which the former Nebraska running back scored at least one touchdown. Previously, he picked up a receiving touchdown in defeat to the Denver Broncos and a rushing touchdown in the 35-12 win over the New York Jets.

With a 7-2 record, the Chiefs narrowly lead the AFC West and look set for a fight to the finish for that top spot against the Broncos.

Africa Moment of the Week: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (Seattle Seahawks)

Smith-Njigba left plenty for the highlights reel with his eight catches totalling 171 yards in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, but nothing could top his third-quarter 71-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the corner.

Largely due to Smith-Njigba's offensive contribution already up until that point, the reigning Super Bowl champions held a slender 14-10 lead when their star wide receiver caught a pass from Drew Lock, dodged a diving tackle attempt from Quay Walker, ran round the outside of Eric Stokes, and went all the way for the touchdown. From there, the Raiders had simply left themselves a mountain too high to climb.

Honorable mentions

Chuba Hubbard - born in Canada but of Nigerian descent - starred with two rushing touchdowns and a total of 172 yards (92 rushing and 80 receiving) in the Carolina Panthers' 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints.

Alvin Kamara - who has family ties to Liberia - scored two touchdowns for the Saints in defeat.

Nigerian-American defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore was the unlikely scorer of a crucial touchdown in the Indianapolis Colts' 24-22 win over the Miami Dolphins.

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, chances for top pick, more
articles.description: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
articles.headlineJa: 2027年NFLドラフト第1巡目の指名順位予想、トップ指名の確率など
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNのFootball Power Indexが、2027年NFLドラフト第1巡目の指名順位を予測。各チームがトップ5、トップ10、そして第1位で指名できる確率も算出している。
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

See more on the NFL draft

First-round picks that have been traded:

The Jacksonville Jaguars' selection was dealt to the Philadelphia Eagles in the Jordan Davis trade.

The Chicago Bears' selection was dealt to the Tennessee Titans in the Jeffery Simmons trade.

The Green Bay Packers' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade.

The Indianapolis Colts' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade.

The Los Angeles Rams' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade.

The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade.

articles.headline: Oviedo fan handed suspended prison sentence for racist abuse towards Mbappé
articles.description: A person has been given a suspended 11-month prison sentence as well a stadium ban and fined for racist insults directed towards Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé during a LaLiga match at Real Oviedo in August.
articles.headlineJa: ムバッペへの人種差別発言で、オビエドのファンに執行猶予付き禁錮刑
articles.descriptionJa: 8月にレアル・オビエドで行われたラ・リーガの試合中、レアル・マドリードのフォワード、キリアン・ムバッペに対して人種差別的な侮辱を行ったとして、ある人物に執行猶予11ヶ月の禁錮刑、スタジアムへの立ち入り禁止、および罰金が科された。
articles.body:
A person has been given a suspended 11-month prison sentence as well a stadium ban and fined for racist insults directed towards Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé during a LaLiga match at Real Oviedo in August.

Mbappe scored twice in the 3-0 win at the Estadio Carlos Tartiere on August 24.

An individual in the crowd had been identified making sounds and gestures towards France forward Mbappe following his opening goal late in the first half and LaLiga reported the incident to police following the match.

A club statement read: "Real Madrid announces that the Second Section of the Provincial Court of Asturias has today issued a guilty verdict against the individual responsible for the racist insults directed at our player Kylian Mbappé during the match between Real Oviedo and Real Madrid on Aug. 24, 2025 at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium.

"The accused has been sentenced for a hate crime to 11 months in prison, various disqualification penalties, and a financial fine.

"The suspension of the prison sentence is conditional upon the individual not attending football stadiums hosting official sports competitions for a period of two years.

- Has Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior finally put summer transfer saga behind him?

- From Ballon d'Or hopes to Real Madrid bench: Should Liverpool re-sign Trent Alexander-Arnold?

- France beat Türkiye to top group, advance to Nations League quarterfinals

"This ruling adds to the criminal convictions already issued for racist insults against Real Madrid players at the Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas, and Jose Zorrilla stadiums.

"Real Madrid, which has acted as a private prosecutor in this case and continues to do so in others involving similar incidents, reaffirms its commitment to combating racism and eradicating any racist behaviour in football and sports."

articles.headline: Has Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior finally put summer transfer saga behind him?
articles.description: After a summer of transfer uncertainty and a sluggish start to the season, Vinícius Junior is on the comeback trail with Real Madrid and Brazil.
articles.headlineJa: レアル・マドリードのヴィニシウス・ジュニオールは、ついに夏の移籍騒動を乗り越えたのか？
articles.descriptionJa: 夏の移籍を巡る不透明な状況とシーズン序盤の不調を経て、ヴィニシウス・ジュニオールはレアル・マドリードとブラジル代表で復活への道を歩んでいる。
articles.body:
Vinícius Júnior has earned hundreds of millions of euros thanks to his feet. Thunderous goals off his instep, intuitive, imaginative crosses bending in from his outstep, defender-fooling step-overs while full-tilt sprinting at 35kmh. The Real Madrid and Brazil star is a winger who's often been a few steps ahead of opponents.

But the metaphorical "first step" that the 26-year-old took in Singapore on Monday -- starting to solve a problem by admitting that there has been one -- might be the best foot forward he's taken in many months.

You've probably consumed his words by now -- with the same hunger as he appears to have consumed summer treats that the regular Joe is allowed but are next to prohibited for elite athletes. Most especially if, simultaneously, they are skimping on the high-intensity, calorie-burning exercise which is now the regimented, obligatory companion of any top footballer during the brief summer weeks when they're not training and playing.

"I don't think I prepared myself well enough for the new season," Vinícius said. "I took advantage of the holidays to rest, to disconnect from soccer and to spend more family time. The final result was that I trained less than in previous summers."

- Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt

- As Nike replaces Adidas, is Champions League star ball on its way out?

- 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's soccer players ... again!

Maybe Vinícius received a timely call from Eden Hazard, the last star to arrive back for a Real Madrid preseason carrying much more weight than is permissible? I'm being fanciful, but wouldn't it be nice to think that one ex-magician might be looking out for a current wing-wizard? Because the Belgian, who still lives in Madrid and remains under the romantic spell of the greatest club in the world (I know because he told me so), is a good morality tale for his Brazilian successor.

"I wouldn't say I was overdoing what I ate -- I just wasn't paying attention," Hazard admitted to L'Equipe soon after he retired from football in 2023, relinquishing a full year of a multi-million contract with Madrid. "I didn't attach any importance to it. I'm a bon vivant; I enjoy eating with friends, having a drink. Dieting sucks -- it's useless ... well, I suppose it's fine if you want to keep playing until you're 40.

"That summer when I arrived at Madrid, I had just finished an incredible season with Chelsea. I told myself, 'Now that I'm at Real, this might be one of the last vacations where I can ... so, I just let myself go."

It cost Hazard acceleration, sharpness of those quick feet of his, injury avoidance, injury recuperation, the faith of his coach, the fans and the media. Reading those words, do you recognise the comparisons with much of Vinícius' season thus far?

Now, Vinícius is a universe away from what became Hazard's extreme situation. But the Brazilian is currently in direct competition for his place on Madrid's left wing with €125 mil

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye USMNT's McKennie amid Pochettino arrival

articles.body:
Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie, while Atlético Madrid are exploring a deal for Lisandro Martínez.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are interested in United States men's national team midfielder Weston McKennie, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport. Incoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino admires the 28-year-old's versatility after working with him with the USMNT and could seek a reunion at Old Trafford. However, McKennie's club, Juventus, see him as central to head coach Luciano Spalletti's plans and are reluctant to sanction a January departure. His contract runs until June 2030.

- Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is expected to feature prominently among Manchester United's January targets under Pochettino, according to The Telegraph. The incoming head coach wants to strengthen his backline, with Bassey's pace and ability to cover at full back making him an attractive option. The Nigeria international's contract runs until next summer, although Fulham hold an option to extend it by a further 12 months.

- Chelsea continue to track Kerim Alajbegović, having come close to signing him before his summer move to Juventus, La Gazzetta dello Sport has revealed. The Serie A giants are determined to resist any efforts to lure him away from Turin. Alajbegović, 19, is contracted until 2031 and remains -- much like McKennie -- a key member of Spalletti's Juve squad. At this stage, no formal negotiations have taken place between the two clubs.

- Atlético Madrid are exploring a January move for Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez, as per TEAMtalk. Diego Simeone's side are attracted by the prospect of pairing the 28-year-old with his Argentine teammate Cristian Romero, although Barcelona are also interested. Martínez has indicated he wants to leave United in 2027 and favours a move to Spain, with the Premier League club open to his departure as they look to reshape their squad.

- Brighton & Hove Albion, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are pursuing Juventus midfielder Adin Licina ahead of January, Tuttosport reports. The teenager is on loan at Cremonese, and Juventus remain reluctant to let him leave permanently before assessing his potential at Serie A level. Bayern Munich retain a preferential right and a 30% share of any future transfer fee.

OTHERS

- Everton are among the clubs interested in Flamengo winger Samuel Lino. The 26-year-old Brazilian is also attracting attention from Roma, Napoli, Juventus and Paris Saint-Germain, although Flamengo view him as an important part of their plans. (4-4-2 via Liverpool Echo)

- Manchester United could face competition from the likes of Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur if they make a winter swoop for Brentford captain Nathan Collins. The Republic of Ireland international is on United's Janua
